text:
Adam Wilsby has become one of the quiet reasons Nashville looks like a different team. The 26-year-old Swede, a fourth-round pick in 2020, is playing 20 minutes a night, and the ice tilts when he's out there: the Predators take 54% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, nearly 11 points better than when he sits. His ice time keeps climbing, up to 28 and a half minutes in Thursday's win in Vegas.

The box score doesn't show it yet. Seven points in 20 games, one goal (an empty-netter in Los Angeles), and almost no power-play time. And the team results around him are, if anything, a little generous: his teammates have scored about six more goals than their chances with him on.

What's real is the skating. He's in the 98th percentile for top speed, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 53% of his entries last season and reaching the slot more than almost any defenseman. Watch for a guy who leaves the zone with the puck and keeps going.
